event.summary: Startup treats old terminals as ended even if ending the server fails
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: an old agent can keep running while its session is shown as interrupted; Restart could start a second agent in the same folder. Details: startup takes OldTerminals::end_private_server without propagating a failure, disables the tmux driver, and reload always treats TerminalKind::Tmux as absent (core.rs:6436-6443, 6970). The no-sentinel branch converts live old rows with TerminalEnded (7099-7116). Suggested bucket: could-be-highest because two agents in one working directory could conflict and lose work; that downstream loss is not established here. Confidence: source-confirmed intended fallback, not execution-observed. proposed_drop: specification acceptance requires independent check. Exact SPEC.md:3014-3016 text: 'A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.' SPEC_impl.md:2997-2999 likewise explicitly accepts this fallback. possible_cover: exact specification acceptance above; no queue or excluded coverage sources searched. Caveat: no runtime reproduction requested or run; inspect other contracts for unintended routes separately.

event.summary: Old-agent cleanup does not select the session's host tabs
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: checked whether ending an old agent also destroys shell tabs that have already moved to terminal hosts; source does not establish that route. Details: core.rs:7337-7338 calls old.sweep with only converted old-kind agent rows. core/old_terminals.rs:300-313 passes SweepTarget::AgentOnly with the recorded agent scope and server-pane roots, never WholeSession. service/sweep.rs:252-260 requires the session marker and selects only the matching agent marker or the legacy shape with neither agent nor tab marker, so ordinary host-tab processes are excluded. old_terminals.rs:399-401 excludes tab scope units when the host tab launch record exists. SPEC.md:3013-3014 says 'A session whose agent or tabs already run in terminal hosts keeps them.' Suggested bucket: could-be-highest if host tabs were accidentally killed, because shell processes and user work could be lost; the selection-based route considered here is refuted. Confidence: source-confirmed refutation for normally marked tabs and readable host records, not execution-observed. proposed_drop: source refutation above. possible_cover: none searched. Caveats: deliberately scrubbed markers or unreadable/missing tab records are different failure modes, not established by this check; this does not claim every callee is defect-free.

event.summary: Old-agent cleanup does not select ordinary host tabs
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: checked whether ending an old agent also destroys shell tabs that already run in terminal hosts; the ordinary shipped launch and record lifecycle exclude those tabs. Original strongest concern preserved: an unintended host-tab kill could lose shell processes and user-owned work, so could-be-highest is yes if such a route is established. Details: core.rs:7337-7338 calls old.sweep. old_terminals.rs:300-313 uses AgentOnly, the recorded agent scope and roots under the old server's agent pane, never WholeSession. sweep.rs:252-260 selects a matching agent marker or the legacy session-only shape with neither kind marker. Additional checks this turn: core.rs:14690-14697 explicitly assigns the tab's session and fresh tab marker; host_tabs.rs:418 mints that tab id and 421 supplies this environment; host_launch.rs:137-161 overlays it into the host child's environment; launch.rs:1289-1303 removes the agent marker before execing the shell and preserves the tab marker. Thus an ordinary host-tab shell is not in the AgentOnly selection. old_terminals.rs:399-401 excludes scope-discovered tabs whenever symlink_metadata sees their host record, even if record contents are unreadable. host_tabs.rs:653-686 writes that record before starting.finish delivers the child spec. Its removal follows confirmed host ending at 860-865 and 1039-1059; 901-910 describes this gate. This supplies ordinary evidence for both the marker and record premises rather than assuming them. SPEC.md Terminal experience says 'A session whose agent or tabs already run in terminal hosts keeps them.' Suggested bucket: other as a refuted concern; highest if the original unintended-kill route were established. Confidence: source-confirmed refutation for ordinary correctly launched and recorded host tabs, not execution-observed. proposed_drop: source refutation above, subject to parent's independent judgment; no parent drop accepted. possible_cover: none searched. Caveats: old_terminals.rs:400 treats every metadata error as absence, so an I/O error could still misclassify a scoped host tab; no ordinary shipped action causing that error on an otherwise healthy retained host record was established. Deliberately scrubbing the tab marker or deleting its record remains outside this ordinary-path refutation. No claim that all callees or filesystem failures are safe. Revision: supplied ordinary launch and removal evidence requested by parent; preserved the original loss-of-work concern and narrowed the conclusion to what source establishes.

event.summary: Snapshot-owner PID reuse can bypass host-tab exclusion
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. Original TLDR/strongest concern preserved: old-terminal startup cleanup can unintentionally stop an already-host-backed shell tab and lose its processes or user-owned work. Could-be-highest: yes; suggested bucket: highest for the conditional wrong-target termination route. This is reconciliation of received g097/l4, not a newly discovered independent issue. Actual source checks: old_terminals.rs:457 records pid/ppid/start identities, :464 reads the current environment of each old direct-child pid with no intervening start-identity check, and :473-476 associates the stale subtree identities with that current owner. If a short-lived old pane exits/is reaped and its number is reassigned to a newly started host-tab child, the new session/tab markers can enter PaneOwner::Tab. Ordinary shipped marker premises were checked in the prior c2 revision: core.rs:14690-14697 and host_tabs.rs:629-641 inject the session and tab UUIDs, and launch.rs:1289-1303 removes the agent marker before shell exec. The direct owner list at old_terminals.rs:369-375 bypasses the retained-host-record exclusion at :399-401. The call from assigned core.rs:7338 therefore reaches old_terminals.rs:329-342, which names the misattributed session/tab's scope and exact marker, even though sweep.rs:1595-1646 discards the reused old root as Ok(None); marker/scope discovery continues. Server-process verification at old_terminals.rs:223-277 gates using any subtree and correctly discards AlreadyGone/mismatch/timeout cases, but does not validate each child's owner identity. Confidence: source-confirmed conditional route; no actual PID reuse, termination or work loss observed. Prior ordinary-path refutation is retained and narrowed: accurate attribution plus AgentOnly and retained host records protect normal tabs. It does not refute this separate owner-misattribution path; neither unreadable record contents nor deliberate marker tampering is needed. proposed_drop: only possible bounded-PID-race acceptance, pending independent interpretation; no parent drop accepted. Exact SPEC_impl.md:5431-5435: 'Process-number reuse inside a short window is accepted, for now.' and 'Code that signals or adopts a process by its number may lose the race in which that process exits and the kernel hands the number to an unrelated process within a short, bounded window: between reading a number and checking it, between reaping a child and signalling its group, while a watchdog fires just as its child finishes, or during a polling loop of at most a few seconds.' Exact exclusion at :5438-5439: 'What is not accepted is carrying a bare number across unbounded waits or asynchronous work, or storing it for later.' The accepted-result window here is bounded by the absolute 15-second old-terminal deadline at :204-233, longer than the few-second polling example; child owner attribution itself runs synchronously, whereas the resulting owner is used later after reload work. These boundaries must be judged independently rather than treating rarity as a refutation. possible_cover: g097/l4 is the same snapshot-owner cause; preserve both IDs/provenance for parent deduplication. No prohibited coverage sources, runtime tests or reproductions. All readily checkable source premises examined; close the renewed c2 lead as this finding. No claim that the separate metadata-error caveat or every cleanup path is defect-free.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. Details: launch_artifacts.rs:273-281 includes all live states in sentinel_could_still_apply. core.rs:7061-7095 checks a direct sentinel before the new TerminalEnded arm at 7100-7114; unreadable sentinels defer reconciliation at 7191-7212. Artifact cleanup runs only after a committed Interrupted result at 7374-7378, or committed Error at 7343-7353. store.rs:386-392 and Transition::apply preserve terminal_address for TerminalEnded. event.summary: Timed-out retirement does not leave a fresh marker sweep running
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. Original strongest concern preserved: a retirement sweep continuing after its timeout might select a replacement generation by the same session marker, kill its new agent and lose user-owned work (could-be-highest: yes if established). Cancellation therefore discards an eventual enumeration result instead of resuming the dropped future to signal a replacement.
